subject: video-assembly
a: the ladder's rung 3 says only that two anchors must be cut from one cloth, so a heterogeneous anchor pair reads as a defect and the producer is told not to do it
b: the amended rung names a third row - two unmistakably different spaces render as a CUT, not a broken interpolation - and gates it on one question: does the assembly need to own this cut point
read_from: three cases walked over the shipped Glass Harbor project (app/_studio/scenes.ts, 5 scenes, 31s): (1) sc-2 INT. CRANE CAB -> sc-3 EXT. ROOFTOP is the story's act-two turn and the Cut derives its marker by scanning SCENES for /turn/i and accumulating targetS - merging the two into one two-world generation either moves the marker off 13s or removes sc-3 from the list and returns null, drawing no marker at all; (2) sc-4 -> sc-5 EXT. WATERLINE - DAWN is the largest world gap in the project and sc-5 is the one scene with pickedFrameId:null, the only readiness signal there is - a clip spanning both leaves sc-5 unpickable while its footage exists; (3) TimelineClip carries one offsetMs and the sync bench nudges the whole block, so a model-chosen cut inside a clip is uncorrectable - the defect is intra-clip and the only affordance is whole-clip
instrument: none needed - the three predictions are read off the shipped scene list and the Cut's own derivation, not from a run
return_condition: re-test as mode=code when the studio grows a generative-video request path with frame anchoring; today lib/ has no video generation at all
note: AMENDMENT, not the whole technique: 'Rung 3 across two worlds'. The verdict is better because the amendment converts an accidental prohibition into a stated trade - rung 3 as it stood gave the right answer (don't pair two worlds) for the wrong reason (it will break), and that reason dies the first time a producer sees a two-world pair come back looking good. STRUCTURAL FACT, undesigned: gravity has no video generation, yet its data model already cannot express the thing the amendment warns about - Scene carries exactly one pickedFrameId and TimelineClip is one span with one start and one duration, so a clip containing its own cut is unrepresentable. The assembly owning every cut is not a policy here; it is a shape.

subject: image-prompt-composition
a: references travel as an unroled bag - GenerateRequest.references?: ImageRef[] where ImageRef is {base64, mime, width?, height?} - and the file header scopes them to 'approved style references'
b: where two references merge in one frame the beats author the interaction (how the subject meets the plate's light, floor, scale, atmosphere), because that relation is in neither reference
read_from: three cases from the shipped tree: (1) the TRANSFER_SCENES style-transfer path in lib/foundry/extract/prompts.ts carries ONE reference plus a text scene - both arms are identical and the amendment correctly changes nothing, which is its range; (2) app/api/imaging/edit/route.ts is the one endpoint with two image inputs (EditRequest{image, instruction, references?}) and is where a subject-into-plate merge would land - arm B adds the relation clause to `instruction`, and judging the result needs generation spend plus a grader, so it was not run; (3) the readback vocabulary splits every observation into `look` (rendering, nothing depicted) and `depiction` (subject and staging) over OBSERVABLE_FIELDS' eleven single-image properties, and types.ts says so in its own comment - 'What the vision model reads back off ONE image'
instrument: the foundry verdict grader (app/api/foundry/runs/[id]/verdicts/route.ts) run over composite calls - which requires the studio to make composite calls at all, and today it makes none
return_condition: when a subject reference and a location plate are attached to one generate/edit call anywhere in the tree
note: AMENDMENT: 'The seam between two references belongs to neither'. Not not-better - the technique did not lose, its precondition is absent: nothing here merges two references in one frame. STRUCTURAL FACT, undesigned: the look/depiction split is a BINARY over one image, so a relation between two images has no slot in it - a composite that is correctly styled and correctly staged and still reads as pasted would be invisible to every field the readback carries. Nobody designed that blind spot; it fell out of the module being single-image.
